display_name: M. Visvesvaraya & Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV (KRS Era)
one_line: Engineer-statesman M. Visvesvaraya and Maharaja Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV overseeing the Krishna Raja Sagara dam in early 20th-century Mysore.

appearance.age_look: Both appear in their late 40s to early 50s, lean and upright; Visvesvaraya slightly thinner and sharper, Wodeyar broader-shouldered with a regal posture.
appearance.face: Visvesvaraya has an angular face, medium-brown South Indian complexion, straight nose, thin lips, light crow’s-feet at the eyes, and a calm, calculating gaze; default expression serious but kind. Wodeyar has a softer oval face, similar medium-brown complexion, fuller cheeks, neat moustache, and a dignified, composed expression with gentle, observant eyes.
appearance.hair: Visvesvaraya’s hair is almost fully white, cut short and close to the scalp, fully covered by a tall Mysore-style white pagri (turban) with a faint cream band; Wodeyar’s hair is black, neatly combed back, mostly hidden beneath an off-white Mysore royal turban with a subtle gold border and a small central gold brooch but no feather.
appearance.costume: Visvesvaraya wears an early 20th-century engineer-bureaucrat outfit: a well-pressed mid-grey woollen Western-style suit (single-breasted, three buttons), white cotton dress shirt, slim black tie, and simple black leather lace-up shoes; beneath the suit hem, plain off-white cotton socks peek slightly. Wodeyar wears a Mysore royal court dress of the same era: an off-white silk angarkha-style long coat reaching mid-calf with a wrap front and subtle vertical jacquard weave, edged with a thin gold piping; underneath, a pale cream kurta and straight off-white churidar trousers; around his waist a broad deep-maroon silk cummerbund-style sash wraps twice and ties on the left with soft folds; on his feet, cream-coloured leather mojari-style shoes with a modest upward curve at the toe, decorated with fine gold stitching. Both are fully and modestly covered in these era-accurate garments.
appearance.signature: A large rolled engineering blueprint tube of the Krishna Raja Sagara dam in Visvesvaraya’s left hand and a polished wooden walking cane with a simple gold-capped handle in Wodeyar’s right hand, both often held or gestured with together as they survey the dam.

ref_desc: A medium-brown-skinned duo: white-haired Visvesvaraya in a mid-grey Western suit, white shirt, black tie and white Mysore turban holding a rolled dam blueprint, alongside Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV in an off-white silk angarkha, maroon waist sash, cream churidar, royal turban and gold-capped wooden cane, all in grey, off-white, maroon, black and gold tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two Indian historical men from early 20th-century Mysore standing side by side against a subtle suggestion of a large masonry dam, showing them clearly head to toe with consistent costumes, colours and props: first, M. Visvesvaraya, lean and angular with a medium-brown South Indian complexion, sharp calm eyes and light age lines, wearing a neatly pressed mid-grey single-breasted suit, white cotton dress shirt, slim black tie, and black leather lace-up shoes, his almost fully white hair cropped short and completely covered by a tall white Mysore-style turban with a faint cream band, holding a large rolled engineering blueprint tube of the dam under his left arm; second, Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV, slightly broader with a medium-brown complexion, softer oval face and neat black moustache, dressed in an off-white silk angarkha-style long coat with subtle vertical texture and thin gold piping, over a pale cream kurta and off-white churidar trousers, his waist wrapped with a deep maroon silk cummerbund sash, feet in cream mojari shoes with light gold embroidery, and his black hair mostly hidden under an off-white Mysore royal turban with a slim gold border and a small central gold brooch, holding a polished wooden walking cane with a gold-capped handle in his right hand; keep both fully and modestly clothed, use a restrained palette of mid-grey, off-white, deep maroon, black and gold, and emphasize consistent anime-style facial features, hairstyles, outfits and props for use across many panels.
